title: Rear-Flank Downdraft (RFD) Climatology & Tornadogenesis
subtitle: The essential role of the RFD in delivering vertical vorticity to ground level

card1.title: THE RFD TORNADOGENESIS HYPOTHESIS
bullets: Crosswise horizontal vorticity generated by environmental wind shear is tilted into the vertical by the main supercell updraft.
An updraft alone cannot bring vertical vorticity down to the surface; it only pulls air upward away from the ground.
The Rear-Flank Downdraft descends behind the updraft, carrying vertical vorticity directly to the ground surface.

card2.title: SURFACE GUST FRONT CONVERGENCE
bullets: As cold RFD air hits the surface, it spreads out, creating an intense arc-shaped convergence boundary.
The RFD curls cyclonically around the updraft, trapping high-circulation air in a shrinking convergence zone.
When RFD convergence meets the main updraft base, rapid vortex contraction spawns the tornado.

notes:
PROFESSOR'S LECTURE NOTES - SLIDE 26 (RFD CLIMATOLOGY & TORNADOGENESIS):
Observational meteorology over the past 30 years has proved conclusively that an updraft alone cannot produce a tornado. An updraft transports vorticity upward, away from the surface. Tornadogenesis requires a downdraft—specifically the Rear-Flank Downdraft—to transport angular momentum and vorticity downward to the ground, where surface friction can concentrate it.

title: Thermodynamic Vulnerability of the Cold RFD Air Mass
subtitle: The 'Goldilocks' paradox: Why excessive cold suppresses tornadogenesis

card1.title: THE COLD POOL PARADOX
bullets: Tornadic supercells exhibit relatively warm RFDs (Δθ ≈ -1 to -3 K); non-tornadic supercells exhibit excessively cold RFDs (Δθ < -6 K).
Excessively cold, dense air cannot be lifted by the updraft; it surges forward as a runaway outflow boundary, cutting off the inflow.
The RFD must be cool enough to descend, but warm enough to be ingested and stretched by the updraft.

card2.title: THE AEOLUS EXPLOITATION STRATEGY
bullets: Because tornadogenesis requires an exquisitely balanced RFD buoyancy profile, the RFD is an extreme thermodynamic vulnerability.
By heating the descending RFD air mass by +3K, AEOLUS destroys its negative buoyancy entirely.
The RFD turns positively buoyant, halts downward momentum transport, and decouples the surface vortex from the supercell engine.

notes:
PROFESSOR'S LECTURE NOTES - SLIDE 27 (RFD THERMODYNAMIC VULNERABILITY):
Here is the core thermodynamic insight of Project AEOLUS: the 'Goldilocks' problem discovered during the VORTEX projects. If an RFD is too cold, it surges away like a snowplow and fails to produce a tornado. If it is too warm, it won't descend. By injecting +3K into the RFD, we push its buoyancy across the threshold, turning downdraft into buoyant lift and arresting the tornadic cycle.

bullets: In a mature tornado, intense tangential velocities (u_θ > 80 m/s) centrifuge raindrops and debris radially outward.
Centrifuged hydrometeors accumulate in a dense annular ring at r ≈ 1.2 · r_core, visible as a hook echo on Doppler radar.
Evaporation occurs predominantly in this outer ring, reinforcing the annular radial temperature gradient.

card2.title: CORE CONTRACTION DYNAMICS
bullets: The horizontal temperature gradient between the dry core and the wet annular ring generates horizontal baroclinic vorticity: ∇θ × ∇p.
This baroclinic vorticity is tilted into the vertical as it enters the core, accelerating rotation.
Disrupting the annular temperature gradient disrupts this continuous baroclinic vorticity feeding mechanism.

In a violent vortex, centrifugal acceleration acts as a giant centrifuge, flinging heavy raindrops and hail out of the core into an annular ring. This ring becomes a site of intense evaporation, creating strong horizontal temperature gradients. Through the baroclinic term ∇θ × ∇p, this temperature gradient continuously generates new vorticity that is ingested into the core.

title: The Fundamental Vulnerability: Ground Boundary Layer Angular Momentum Flux
subtitle: Why tornadoes cannot survive without continuous surface angular momentum replenishment

card1.title: THE VORTEX AS AN OPEN SYSTEM
bullets: A tornado is not a self-contained rotating top; it is an open dissipative thermodynamic engine.
Turbulent viscosity and upward convective ejection continually expel angular momentum through the top of the vortex column.
The core survives solely because strong radial inflow (u_r < 0) in the lowest 200m continually sweeps high angular momentum inward to the core.

card2.title: THE AEOLUS EXPLOITATION PARADIGM
bullets: Instead of attacking the 90 m/s winds at the core, attack the fragile boundary-layer inflow pipeline feeding it.
Brute force seeks to cancel 10¹² J of rotational energy. AEOLUS simply pinches the fuel line.
Once boundary-layer replenishment is severed, internal turbulent dissipation collapses the core within seconds.

notes:
PROFESSOR'S LECTURE NOTES - SLIDE 31 (GROUND FLUX VULNERABILITY):
The defining theoretical breakthrough of Project AEOLUS is treating the tornado as an open dissipative system. A tornado continuously radiates angular momentum upward and outward. It maintains its terrifying intensity only because the surface boundary layer acts as a pipeline, pumping fresh angular momentum into the base. If we cut that pipeline, the vortex core starves and dissipates naturally.

In fluid dynamics, symmetric vortices are notoriously resistant to axisymmetric (m=0) perturbations. If you blow or suck symmetrically, the vortex simply adjusts its radius. But if you apply an asymmetric force over a single quadrant (m=1 or m=2), you excite elliptic and dipolar instabilities. These non-axisymmetric modes deform the circular streamlines into an ellipse, triggering rapid vortex breakdown.

title: Thermal RFD Intervention Physics: +3K Buoyancy Injection

The thermal intervention injects a +3K potential temperature anomaly into the descending rear-flank downdraft. title: Mathematical Formulation of Thermal RFD Intervention
subtitle: Discretization in interventions/thermal_rfd.py and coupling into solver.py
codeText:
class ThermalRFDIntervention:
    def __init__(self, delta_theta=3.0, z_max=800.0, theta_min=np.pi/2, theta_max=np.pi):
        self.delta_theta = delta_theta  # +3.0 K injection
        self.z_max = z_max              # Surface to 800m AGL
        self.theta_range = (theta_min, theta_max)  # Rear-flank quadrant

    def apply(self, grid, current_theta, dt):
        # Spatial mask for rear-flank quadrant within boundary layer
        mask = (grid.z_coords <= self.z_max) & \
               (grid.theta_coords >= self.theta_range[0]) & \
               (grid.theta_coords <= self.theta_range[1])
        # Additive thermal anomaly with smooth exponential taper
        current_theta[mask] += self.delta_theta * (1.0 - grid.z_coords[mask] / self.z_max) * dt

card.title: ALGORITHMIC IMPLEMENTATION
bullets: Confined to θ ∈ [π/2, π] (90° to 180°), matching the rear-flank quadrant of cyclonic supercells.
Confined to the lowest 800 meters, where the descending RFD interacts with the ground boundary layer.
Tapers from 100% at the surface (z = 0) to 0% at z = 800m, maximizing thermal impact at ground level.
Applied incrementally per time step to avoid numerical shock waves in the Poisson solver.

notes:

Here is the exact implementation from interventions/thermal_rfd.py. We target the rear-flank quadrant, θ between π/2 and π, from the surface up to 800 meters. The thermal anomaly is tapered linearly with height so that maximum heating occurs at ground level where the cold pool is densest. This smooth application prevents acoustic shocks while ensuring robust numerical stability.

title: Tangential Momentum Sink Physics: Off-Axis Placement Dynamics

card1.title: WHY ON-AXIS SUCTION FAILS
bullets: Applying vacuum directly on the central axis (r = 0) deepens the core pressure deficit.
A deeper core pressure deficit accelerates radial inflow (u_r < 0), pulling even more angular momentum inward.
On-axis suction paradoxically strengthens the vortex, increasing peak core winds!

card2.title: WHY OFF-AXIS SUCTION SUCCEEDS
bullets: Off-axis suction at r = 750m exerts a powerful external counter-torque: τ = r × F_sink.
Captures angular momentum at large radii where specific angular momentum L = r·u_θ is highest.
Pulls the vortex center toward the suction source, creating destructive tilt and elliptic shear.

notes:
PROFESSOR'S LECTURE NOTES - SLIDE 38 (OFF-AXIS DYNAMICS):
This is a critical hydrodynamic distinction: if you place a vacuum on the central axis, you actually accelerate the tornado. Why? Because you deepen the central pressure well, which sucks more air into the base and spins the core faster. Off-axis placement at r = 750m captures the angular momentum at the periphery and exerts an external torque that twists the core apart.

title: Mathematical Formulation of Momentum Sink in solver.py
subtitle: Implementation in interventions/momentum_sink.py and Navier-Stokes forcing
codeText:
class MomentumSinkIntervention:
    def __init__(self, delta_p=-47.80, r_range=(500.0, 1000.0), theta_range=(0.0, np.pi/2), z_max=200.0):
        self.delta_p = delta_p          # -47.80 Pa calibrated vacuum
        self.r_range = r_range          # Outer core inflow zone
        self.theta_range = theta_range  # Quadrant 1 (0 to 90 deg)
        self.z_max = z_max              # Ground boundary layer (0-200m)

    def apply(self, grid, u_r, u_theta, dt):
        # Active boundary layer mask
        mask = (grid.r_coords >= self.r_range[0]) & (grid.r_coords <= self.r_range[1]) & \
               (grid.theta_coords >= self.theta_range[0]) & (grid.theta_coords <= self.theta_range[1]) & \
               (grid.z_coords <= self.z_max)
        # Enforce tangential drag deceleration and radial redirection
        drag_coeff = abs(self.delta_p) / 100.0  # Normalized drag
        u_theta[mask] *= np.exp(-drag_coeff * dt)
        u_r[mask] *= 0.10  # 90% boundary layer surface blackout!

card.title: FORCING TENSOR COMPONENTS
bullets: u_θ decaus exponentially: u_θ^(n+1) = u_θ^n · exp(-k_drag · Δt), extracting rotational kinetic energy.
u_r is attenuated by 90%, blocking the radial transport of circulation into the core.
Targets the lowest boundary layer where ground friction already weakens centrifugal resistance.
Exponential damping guarantees unconditional stability regardless of time step size.

notes:
PROFESSOR'S LECTURE NOTES - SLIDE 39 (MOMENTUM SINK MATHEMATICS):
In interventions/momentum_sink.py, the momentum sink operates via two coupled terms. First, tangential velocity u_θ is damped exponentially based on the vacuum setpoint ΔP = -47.80 Pa. Second, radial velocity u_r is multiplied by 0.10, representing a 90% boundary layer surface blackout that completely cuts off the radial circulation flux.
